text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- On Youth and Sport Day holiday the most important message is the call of modern Turkey's founder Mustafa Kemal Ataturk for youth to protect the secular system.
- Turkish youth is being crushed by poor working conditions or unemployment, making up 70 percent of the total unemployed.
- A week of destiny for the government. The Islamist-led coalition has been pushed into a corner by a censure motion set for possible debate this week.
- Developments in the defence industry are to be discussed at a conference in Istanbul in June.
- A far-right party's congress to choose a new leader is postponed for a month after disputes erupt at a weekend meeting.
- The Anadolu Group plans to develop a private health project modelled on examples in the United States.
- Leftist leader Bulent Ecevit says democracy is in danger and the ruling Islamists are encouraging the military to carry out a coup.
- A commission is to be established to implement a law aimed at curbing money laundering.
- Requests are flooding in for the newly formed competition council to carry out investigations into matters such as promotions, the cement industry and bread prices.
- Celebrations are to be held throughout the country for Youth and Sport Day and more than 100,000 people are expected to attend a pro-secularist concert in Ankara.
